newsitem.title: USA: Church, U.S. priest ordered to pay $120 million.
newsitem.headline: Church, U.S. priest ordered to pay $120 million.

text.p: The Roman Catholic diocese of Dallas was ordered on Thursday to pay $120 million in damages to 10 former altar boys and the parents of another who were sexually abused by a Catholic priest.
It was by far the largest cash penalty imposed against the Catholic church in a sexual abuse case.

A jury of 10 women and two men said in the civil proceedings that the diocese was guilty of gross negligence, malice, conspiracy and fraud in failing to stop the Rev. Rudolph Kos from abusing the children over an 11-year period ending in 1992, and in covering up evidence when the victims came forward.
The diocese was ordered to pay about $102 million in actual damages and $18 million in punitive damages.
"I hope they wake up the Pope tonight with this," plaintiffs' attorney Sylvia Demarest, told Reuters.
The victims included Jay Lemberger, who committed suicide in 1992 at the age of 20.

"My son was murdered by the Dallas diocese because they let Rudy Kos into their regime and they let him get away with this abuse," said Pat Lemberger, the boy's father. He and his wife Nancy joined the 10 other former altar boys in the lawsuit and were awarded a total of $20.2 million.
The boys, who now range in age from 18 to early 30s, were each awarded between $7.4 and $13.2 million.
When the verdict was read out, the young men hugged each other and their relatives with joy.

Bishop Charles Grahmann said the diocese would likely appeal the verdict "in order that a higher court can review all the issues and make certain that a final verdict is just and appropriate to the facts of the case."
The diocese has argued that Kos decieved everybody, including the boys' families, and pointed out that he was suspended as soon as a first youth complained about sexual abuse in 1992.

Tom Economus, head of a Chicago-based victim support group called "The Linkup: Survivors of clergy sexual abuse," said it was the largest penalty in a church sexual abuse. The previous high was $13 million in a Florida case last year, he said.
Kos, who was suspended from the priesthood in 1992 and is now facing criminal charges of sexual abuse of a child, did not attend the trial. He is 52 and lives in San Diego, California.
Kos was accused of abusing boys as young as nine years old on hundreds of occasions at three different Dallas-area churches, even having regular "sleepovers" in his rectory room.

The former altar boys testified that Kos was like a father to them, but drew them into sexual relationships that began with foot massages and then escalated to masturbation and oral sex. They said he gave them candy and video games and plied them with sedatives, alchohol and marijuana.
"I grew up a very firm Catholic but I just don't feel like I can go to church now," said 28-year-old Lee Hart, who was abused over several years.

Church officials had declined to cut a deal out of court, but said they were humbled by the jury's verdict and its conclusion that the diocese bore even more responsibility for the years of abuse than Kos himself.
"This whole process has been significantly humbling, " said Monsignor John Bell.
